subject: Urgent: Oceana Logistics RTT surge — interzone egress mismatch
messages:
From: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@oceanalogistics.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-11-14T07:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Latency noticed this morning (prod)

Hi Olga / Marissa,

We started seeing a sharp jump in API latency for EU users around 06:30 UTC. p95 jumped from ~140ms to ~480ms and p99 hit ~1s. A number of our batch jobs retried and we observed a ~3% error spike for token generation calls. Can you confirm if there are any ongoing incidents or changes that might explain this?

Attached is a traceroute from one of our EU workers. Happy to jump on a call if helpful.

Thanks,
Alex
Lead Platform Engineer | Oceana Logistics

From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, david.kim@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-11-14T07:35:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Latency noticed this morning (prod) — escalate to SRE/Network

Team, forwarding Oceanalogistics' report — they hit a p95/p99 spike from EU customers. Traceroute looks like traffic from eu-west is egressing via us-east and then returning, adding an extra hop.

Immediate asks:
- David / NetEng: confirm whether any egress mapping or route table change was deployed between 06:00–07:00 UTC that could cause EU tenants to punch out via US egress.
- Karthik: if routing is the cause, can we prepare a rollback plan for the routing policy and an emergency filter to pin eu-west traffic to eu egress?
- Marissa / CS: please loop the customer and offer an update and a short credit if this impacts SLA.

I've added Laura for product visibility (this is a customer-facing P95 regression). If we confirm a misconfiguration, we should prepare an exec summary for Ops/Customer success.

Olga Petrov
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
[attachment: datadog-p95-graph-20281114.png (image)]
From: david.kim@redwood.ai
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-11-14T08:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Latency noticed this morning (prod) — quick triage

On 2028-11-14 07:35 UTC, olga.petrov@redwood.ai wrote:
> Team, forwarding Oceanalogistics' report — they hit a p95/p99 spike from EU customers. Traceroute looks like traffic from eu-west is egressing via us-east and then returning, adding an extra hop.

Confirmed: at ~06:18 UTC an automated route optimizer job deployed a small change to egress selection heuristics (intended to rebalance cost for a subset of low-traffic tenants). That job mistakenly included the eu-west routing pool due to a tag filter bug.

Impact observed in metrics: p50 ~140ms -> 160ms (small), p95 ~140ms -> 480ms, p99 ~320ms -> 980ms. Error rate for generation endpoints increased from 0.9% to ~3.6% during the window. Throughput held steady.

I have rolled back the optimizer change in the staging control plane and queued an emergency rollback to prod. I need 10–15 minutes to coordinate with NetEng to push the route fix and then validate.

Attachments: egress routing diff and current traceroute output.

David Kim
Senior SRE | Redwood Inference
[attachment: egress-routing-diff.patch (patch)]
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
To: david.kim@redwood.ai, olga.petrov@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-11-14T08:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Realtime mitigation plan

Thanks David — prepping an emergency filter now.

Mitigation plan (executing):
1) Apply emergency routing policy to pin tenants with eu tags to eu egress (expected 3–5 min roll).
2) Disable the optimizer job until we push a safer tag filter.
3) Monitor p95/p99 and error rates for Oceanalogistics and a sample of EU tenants for 30 minutes post-fix.
4) If residual errors persist, fall back to circuit-breaker to route customers to secondary replicas in eu region.

I'll push the policy in 2 mins and report back with timings.

Karthik Iyer
Staff Software Engineer, Runtime Routing | Redwood Inference
From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
To: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@oceanalogistics.com>, Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@oceanalogistics.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-11-14T08:20:00Z
Subject: RE: Latency noticed this morning (prod) — quick update

Alex / Sarah — quick update from our side: we detected an unintended egress optimizer deployment that caused some EU traffic to egress via our US pool, adding an extra inter-region hop. Our engineering team is applying an emergency pin to return EU tenants to EU egress now. Expect improvements within ~10 minutes; we will follow up when metrics normalize.

We deeply apologize for the disruption — Marissa will reach out with an interim credit offer and an ETA for the postmortem. If you have any further telemetry to share (traces / request ids), please attach them here.

— Olga
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
From: david.kim@redwood.ai
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, laura.bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Gomez <alex.gomez@oceanalogistics.com>, Sarah Connors <sarah.connors@oceanalogistics.com>
Date: 2028-11-14T09:05:00Z
Subject: Post-fix update / closure

Status: Mitigation applied at 08:23 UTC — emergency pin pushed, optimizer disabled.

Observed after fix: p95 for Oceanalogistics returned to ~150ms within 7 minutes; p99 dropped below 400ms. Error rate returned to baseline within 12 minutes. No further retries observed from their batch jobs.

Next steps:
- Karthik to open a follow-up to harden tag filters and add a pre-deploy canary for optimizer jobs (INF-7821).
- Laura to prepare a short exec summary for the account team and legal; Marissa to send a compensation note and schedule the postmortem call with the customer.
- David to run a retrospective and add an automated alert when optimizer jobs touch >1 region pool.

I'll attach the Datadog chart and traceroute output to the postmortem. Closing this thread once the customer sign-off is captured.

David Kim
Senior SRE | Redwood Inference
